comments.rawMarkdown: Hi Ryan, I noticed you've now reached a 2.25 public score, congrats! I was following this issue because I've also experienced a significant difference between local simulation performance and Kaggle public scores. Did you manage to identify the root cause of the discrepancy? In particular, did you find any meaningful difference between the local SDK environment and the Kaggle server side runtime (game initialization, environment state, runtime, etc.) or was the improvement mainly due to changes in your agent? Any details you can share would be greatly appreciated.

replies.rawMarkdown:
I'm seeing this too. Qwen 3.8 exacerbated this. I am going to try lowering the reasoning to medium tonight. I am wondering if there is some sort of multitenancy contention issue on the shared PCIE bus accessing the assigned GPU when others are doing the same for their assigned GPU from their different cloud instances running virtualized on the same physical machine. 

I believe the HW is 8 GPUs? But they share the same PCIE bus. My local machine is a single RTX Pro 6000 with no other users or tasks.

Last week I was in position 19 BTW. The inability to diagnose this is mind-boggling.

Hi Kaggle staff and ARC team,

  I'm the current Human Leaderboard #1 on ARC-AGI-3
  (FuFront-AI-RyanX-Atlas-AGI, 100.00 / 25 games / 183 levels / 6176 actions),
  verified on arcprize.org/leaderboard.

  My agent reproduces 0.96+ in local simulation using the official
  arc_agi-0.9.8 SDK. Across 6 Kaggle submissions since 2026-04-30,
  my publicScore has been:

  ┌────────────┬─────────────┐
  │    Date    │ publicScore │
  ├────────────┼─────────────┤
  │ 2026-04-30 │ 0.19        │
  ├────────────┼─────────────┤
  │ 2026-05-01 │ 0.00        │
  ├────────────┼─────────────┤
  │ 2026-05-02 │ 0.00        │
  ├────────────┼─────────────┤
  │ 2026-05-03 │ 0.00        │
  ├────────────┼─────────────┤
  │ 2026-05-04 │ 0.00        │
  ├────────────┼─────────────┤
  │ 2026-05-05 │ 0.04        │
  └────────────┴─────────────┘

  Mentioning the leaderboard standing only as a priority signal — I'm
  flagging this because the gap between local-sim and Kaggle-public score
  is large enough that I think it warrants a scoring-infra look rather
  than another agent iteration on my side.

  Capability context (not the main ask)

  This is not a toy replay script. My agent has also solved a separate
  RX185-style challenge that tests source-aware reasoning, phase tracking,
  memory snapshots, and deterministic strategy construction beyond
  ordinary leaderboard trace replay.

  I am not attaching private solver code, traces, or internal tooling
  publicly. If the ARC team wants to verify this capability, I can share
  a redacted RX185 challenge packet or arrange a private reproduction
  channel.

  The reason I mention RX185 is to clarify that the current Kaggle issue
  is unlikely to be explained by "the agent simply cannot solve ARC-style
  environments." The problem I am asking you to inspect is the
  scoring/runtime path: dataset mount, agent invocation, game IDs,
  gateway interaction, timeout, and stderr.

  What I'd like to request

  1. A scoring trace for one of my failed submissions
  (e.g., 2026-05-05, publicScore 0.04): which stage failed
  (parquet load / agent import / SDK call / timeout / CUDA cap),
  with stderr if available.
  2. Confirmation of which artifact is actually scored:
  submission.parquet or my_agent.py?
  3. Documented guidance on locking T4×2 accelerator on
  kaggle kernels push — pushes appear to default to P100, which
  silently breaks INT4/AWQ/FP8 model kernels (sm_75+ required).
  Currently the only workaround I know is the UI flip
  (Settings → Session options → Accelerator → GPU T4×2 → Save & Run All).

  Three observations that suggest scoring-infra rather than agent quality

  These are observations, not proven claims — happy to be corrected:

  - (a) Possible parquet pass-through. Across multiple of my submissions
  with different leaderboard scores, the resulting submission.parquet
  appeared identical in size (2648 bytes). This suggests the scoring
  path may invoke my_agent.py against server-side game instances rather
  than reading the parquet. Could you confirm?
  - (b) P100 vs T4×2 reset on push. As above; reproducible by anyone
  using AWQ/INT4 models.
  - (c) Possible env-hash drift on ka59. In a 24-trace replay audit
  on a server-style runtime, 23/24 PASSed but ka59 FAILed despite
  WIN on the public local SDK. If server-side game instances re-init
  with a different RNG seed than the public SDK exposes, agents that
  infer per-game state could break silently. Can you confirm
  hash-identity policy?

  Account / identifier (public-safe)

  - Kaggle user: ryanxatlasai
  - Competition: arc-prize-2026-arc-agi-3
  - Kernels involved (11 versions): ryanx-agi, ryanx-agi-0501,
  ryanx-agi-0504, r0503-graph-inline-fix, plus
  notebook{ce398f99b8, 2c5a3843d2, 26721c089f, b76fa0bb8c,  06460cfeea, b64ebd4c60, c130988125}.

  I'd prefer to forward my_agent.py, the trace .jsonl, and any
  detailed log via a private secure channel (Kaggle DM, ARC team
  private email, or any escalation route you prefer) rather than attach
  publicly. Please reply with a preferred channel.

  Thanks.

  ---
